scenes.visual: close-up illustration of a hard white plastic anti-theft tag clipped to the hem of a folded blue shirt on a clothes shop table, a small round grey pin dome on one end of the tag, the tag and shirt in the lower two-thirds of the frame, simple soft shop background
scenes.narration: That hard tag on a new shirt... how does the shop door *know*?

scenes.visual: illustration of two tall pale grey security gate panels standing at the entrance of an Indian clothes shop, a young Indian woman with a shopping bag walking out between them and glancing at them curiously, seen from inside the shop, the gates and the woman in the lower two-thirds of the frame
scenes.narration: Yesterday's answer: B, camera or mic. Now, these gates have no camera. So how do they *catch* a tag?
scenes.headline: NO *CAMERA*

scenes.visual: 2D animation: the tag turns see-through and shows a thin metal strip inside; a battery icon gets a red cross
scenes.narration: Open the tag up. No battery, no chip. Just a thin *metal* strip, cut to one exact size.
scenes.headline: ONE *STRIP*

scenes.visual: illustration of a big shiny brass temple bell hanging from a wooden beam at an Indian temple entrance, a hand just moving away from it after striking it, soft curved sound lines spreading out from the bell, plain warm background, the bell in the lower two-thirds of the frame
scenes.narration: Now think of a temple *bell*. Hit it once, and it keeps ringing after your hand is gone.
scenes.headline: LIKE A *BELL*

scenes.visual: 2D animation: a gate panel sends pulses, the strip in the tag wobbles, a counter climbs to 58,000 times a second, then the gate goes quiet and the strip keeps ringing back
scenes.narration: That strip is a tiny bell. The gate sends an invisible *ping*, and the strip rings. Then the gate goes quiet... and *listens*.
scenes.headline: PING... *LISTEN*

scenes.visual: illustration of a bunch of house keys, a smartphone and a few coins lying on a shop counter next to a hard white plastic anti-theft tag, seen from above at a slight angle, simple uncluttered counter, the objects in the lower two-thirds of the frame
scenes.narration: Why listen? Your keys and phone go silent the moment the ping stops. Only a strip cut to the gate's exact note keeps *ringing*.
scenes.headline: ONLY THE TAG *RINGS*

scenes.visual: illustration of the two pale grey security gate panels at a clothes shop door glowing softly, a small red alarm light lit on top of one panel, a paper shopping bag with a folded blue shirt passing between them, seen from the side, the gates in the lower two-thirds of the frame
scenes.narration: So if the gate hears a ring in the quiet... <short pause> it knows a tag is walking out. *Beep*.
scenes.headline: IT *HEARS* THE TAG

scenes.visual: 2D animation: cross-section of the tag on a shirt, a magnet under the counter glows, the little clamp inside pulls apart and the tag lifts free of the pin
scenes.narration: At the till, a strong *magnet* pulls the tiny lock open, and the tag slides off. No tag, no ring, no beep.
scenes.headline: THE TILL *MAGNET*

scenes.narration: These legends got it first. Nicely done!
scenes.narration_none: Nobody cracked yesterday's one... <chuckles> let's see if you can beat today's.
scenes.headline: *SHOUTOUT*

youtube.title: How do anti theft tags work? #shorts
youtube.description:
How do anti theft tags work? Inside that hard security tag on clothes there's no battery, just a thin metal strip cut to one exact size. Think of a temple bell: hit it once and it keeps ringing. The shop security gates send a short invisible magnetic ping, the strip rings back (about 58,000 times a second), then the gate goes quiet and listens. Keys and phones go silent the moment the ping stops; only the tag's strip keeps ringing, so a ring in the quiet means a tag is walking out. At the till, a strong magnet pulls the tag's tiny lock open so it slides off.
